issue_results.result: Confirmed literal tensor-convention/effective-operator defect; Minor retained with a Hamiltonian-preserving normalization.
issue_results.source_and_hypotheses: Physical5/printed1363 states only h=h^T and V_abcd=V_cdab. Equations21,25 and30, physical8,10,18, use J-K. Proposition8 assumes a rank-N projector compatible with the fragments, not A3/A4. The variational impurity is defined by frozen-core restriction in equations12-15.
issue_results.decisive_evidence: For L=4,N=2 and four singleton fragments, D=ones(2)/2 direct-sum ones(2)/2 and h=I-2D satisfy the gap and all fragment ranks, with Lx=1<N. Fragment1 impurity is span(e1,e2), core c=(e3+e4)/sqrt2. Set V_abcd=S_ab A_cd+A_ab S_cd with S13=S31=1,A23=1,A32=-1. Pair-Hermiticity holds. Each term has a symmetric creation or annihilation pair, so the entire interaction operator vanishes by CAR. Nevertheless the raw printed contraction on cc^T has impurity block[[0,1],[0,0]], nonzero and nonsymmetric, and expectation1/2 in the equal superposition.
issue_results.repair_and_core_boundary: Vc_abcd=(V_abcd+V_badc)/2 preserves the many-body operator because the simultaneous swaps produce two minus signs. It also preserves the HF energy and the variational impurity maps. Pair-Hermiticity plus this simultaneous-swap symmetry justifies the self-adjoint J-K contractions. Here Vc=0. Thus a local representative convention, or corresponding symmetrized contractions, repairs the operator formulas without restricting the physical Hamiltonian or A1-A4. A3/A4 were not imposed on an example for a proposition that does not require them.
issue_results.counterevidence: Standard physical tensor conventions may already include this extra symmetry; the source's explicit mathematical hypothesis does not. This is not a counterexample to either main theorem. The exact initial full16-dimensional CAR result is reused with its original execution binding and independently corroborated by the antisymmetry argument.

issue_results.result: Confirmed response sign and chemical-potential denominator errors; Minor retained after reconnecting the factorization to the actual response.
issue_results.source_and_definitions: Physical31 equation54 defines delta spectral projector=-Lplus(delta h). Physical37-39 equations68-76 define B, A, L and the frozen-impurity response to h+Y; A4 on physical10 concerns this true response on the trace-zero block space, not an arbitrarily signed printed expression.
issue_results.independent_derivation: For p_x=C_x^T Pi_x C_x, t=sum_x<p_x,Lplus_x(p_x)> is strictly positive by A2. Differentiating the total trace gives mu'[Y]=sum_x<p_x,Lplus_x(C_x^T Y C_x)>/t=Tr(GY)/t. Thus R[Y]=-sum_x Pi_x C_x Lplus_x(C_x^T Y C_x-mu'[Y]p_x) C_x^T Pi_x. There is no t=1 assumption; its trace is exactly zero.
issue_results.hypothesis_compliant_witness: For u=(1,1,1,1)/2, v=(1,3,-2,-2)/sqrt18, D=uu^T+vv^T and h=I-2uu^T-3vv^T, the spectrum is(-2,-1,1,1) and populations(11/36,3/4,17/36,17/36). Every off-diagonal D entry is nonzero, so a commuting diagonal matrix is scalar and B is onto. Set z_i=p_i(1-p_i), M_ii=z_i,M_ij=-D_ij^2 and positive inverse impurity gaps sigma=(11/24,3/8,17/42,17/42). The actual response is -2 sigma_i[(My)_i-mu'z_i]. If it vanishes, summing My=mu'z gives mu'=0 and connectedness of the Laplacian M makes y constant; hence A4 holds on trace zero. For y=(1,-1,0,0), n=95/1512,t=6701/9072,mu'=570/6701, while the printed response trace is n(1-t)=225245/13716864, nonzero.
issue_results.core_repair: The positive Hessian has occupied-to-virtual block action X->h_plus X-Xh_minus. For Q=A^-1 B*Y, the expression(70) becomes the corrected negative response because [D0,[h,Q]]=-B*Y; the trace condition supplies n/t. Therefore dPhi=R(BA^-1 B*)^-1 remains valid. A>0 and B onto make BA^-1B* positive; A4 then gives the required invertibility. Both sign and denominator matter. The finite-dimensional analytic LL/HL maps and local IFT reconnect without a new main-theorem counterexample.
issue_results.scope: The two-sided small-alpha and near-D0 quantifiers were checked. No global uniqueness, uniform interval, or convergence of fixed-point iteration is claimed.

issue_results.result: Confirmed wrong-product surjectivity diagnostic and unresolved printed dimension conventions; Minor retained.
issue_results.source_and_evidence: Physical14 states Nf=3,Lx=2,dimY=8 and N=10; by the real one-particle definitions this would give L=6<N. Physical15 Figure6 and text call the smallest eigenvalue of B*B a surjectivity test. In the all-A1-A4 example above dimT=4,dimY=3, B is onto, but Q=[[0,0,3,-3],[0,0,5,-5],[3,5,0,0],[-3,-5,0,0]] is nonzero, tangent and has BdQ=0. Indeed Q=a b^T+b a^T with a=(3,5,0,0) in RanD and b=(0,0,1,-1) in KerD. Thus B*B has zero minimum eigenvalue even though A3 holds.
issue_results.counterevidence_and_boundary: The theoretical criterion in Lemma11 and equation41, physical20 and27, correctly uses injectivity of the adjoint/full target rank. Positive BB* on Y is the correct test. Native color source pages51-52 show five occupied and seven virtual orbitals and a7-by5 block; conditional on those being the real one-particle spaces and equal fragments, L=12,N=5,Lx=4,dimY=29,dimT=35 follows.
issue_results.calibration: Spin or paired-orbital conventions may explain the printed counts, and the Figure5 legend itself uses a population scale2. The actual code/Jacobian convention and corrected numerical curves were not inspected or reproduced; these are clarification limits, not assertions that the implementation is wrong or that absent code is a mathematical defect. The analytical rank theorem is not refuted.

issue_results.result: Confirmed incorrect stated fixed-point bifurcation criterion; Minor retained.
issue_results.source_and_derivation: Physical16/printed1374 describes a simple real eigenvalue of dF0DMET crossing zero with the other eigenvalues having negative real parts, while solving P=F(P). The actual residual is Phi=F-P, explicitly used correctly in equation67 on physical36. Thus dPhi=dF-I: the stated crossing becomes eigenvalue-1 and all remaining eigenvalues stay nonzero. The IFT supplies a unique local solution branch under that spectral condition.
issue_results.counterevidence_and_calibration: A necessary singularity for the fixed-point residual is eigenvalue1 of dF, equivalently0 of dPhi. A residual zero crossing alone also does not establish transcritical normal-form nondegeneracy. Figure8 and AppendixB describe numerical branches; they are not refuted, and no claim is made about which derivative the implementation actually computed. A notational F-versus-Phi substitution is a plausible explanation, explicitly left for clarification. The regime with failed A4 is outside Theorem4.

issue_results.result: Retained confirmed local errors as Minor; two unsupported subclaims withdrawn and corrected in all active report/evidence records.
issue_results.retained_source_errors: Physical24/printed1382 drops the1/2 factor when relabelling the four-contraction a7 sum. Physical35-36 equations64-66 omit the frozen-core contraction and the two-body1/2 in the displayed high-level Hamiltonian and use a double-index sum for total charge. Physical42 inserts an extra1/sqrt(N!) in a canonical CAR Slater product. Physical43's positive intermediate d1_ai displays lose the minus sign from the preceding perturbation formula; equation77 already restores it.
issue_results.independent_witnesses: With the compatible L4,N2 block projector and h=I-2D, canonical V1313=V3131=1 represents n1 n3. Freezing c=(e3+e4)/sqrt2 yields(1/2)n1; the a7 inner four-contraction sum is1, so its prefactor must stay1/2. Canonical V1212=V2121=1 gives n1n2 energy1 at double impurity occupation, compared with2 when its half factor is omitted. For the L6,N3 charge example, P=[[1/2,1/4],[1/4,1/2]], D4=[[P,sqrt3 I/4],[sqrt3 I/4,I-P]], D=D4 direct-sum ones(2)/2, fragments{1,2},{3,5},{4,6}: P(I-P)=3I/16 gives a rank3 projector, fragment spectra(1/4,3/4),(1/2,1/2),(1/2,1/2), Lx2<N, gap spectrum+-1. The actual charge is3; the all-entry sum is7/2. Canonical two-creation-operator norm is1; the extra factor gives norm squared1/2.
issue_results.withdrawn_index_subclaim: Native physical43 image prints J_mn=sum W_npmq d_pq and K_mn=sum W_npqm d_pq. The old script instead used W_mnpq and W_mpnq. For symmetric d and normalized pair-Hermitian W, swapping dummy p,q identifies J with(21), and W_npqm=W_qmnp=W_mqpn identifies K. A genuinely executed focused exact check now gives the same diag(1/2,0,1/2,0) for both definitions in the canonical n1n3 example and the same D1=diag(-1/8,1/8,-1/8,1/8) as the retained full6-by6 Fock solve. The alleged contraction-index counterexample is false and withdrawn.
issue_results.withdrawn_mu_subclaim: The actual physical46/printed1404 image closes the alpha parenthesis after the two-body term, before -mu(alpha). This term is already outside alpha, and the later W1 correctly includes -mu_prime(0). The previously computed nonzero135/6701 does not establish a printed factoring error. That subclaim is withdrawn without discarding its valid numeric calculation.
issue_results.core_repair_and_limits: Restoring the genuinely omitted core/half-factor terms and using the trace charge constraint leaves an analytic finite-Fock Hamiltonian with the same noninteracting gap and positive charge derivative. The scalar IFT therefore yields the correct high-level map locally. Normalizing the determinant and retaining negative excitation denominators gives the singles-only one-body derivative; doubles do not contribute. The core plus occupied impurity projector equals D0, so the true interacting and HF high-level first derivatives agree after matching the charge scalar. Equations78-83 and the invertible residual then give equal block-density derivatives, and the common LL derivative gives full-density equality. Theorems4 and5 are not refuted. Minor is based on these verified local repairs, not on a rule excluding Major whenever a main theorem lacks a counterexample.
